title: Learning Fair Representation via Distributional Contrastive Disentanglement

problem.claim: Fair representation learning aims to achieve fairness or debias sensitive information while retaining predictive information.

gap.claim: Existing adversarial representation-learning methods can have unstable training, potentially harming the balance between fairness and predictiveness.

contributions.claim: FarconVAE disentangles the latent space into sensitive and non-sensitive parts using distributional contrastive learning.
The approach constructs observation pairs with different sensitive attributes but identical labels and contrasts their latent distributions.
The paper introduces a distributional contrastive loss motivated by Gaussian and Student-t kernels and provides theoretical analysis.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present FarconVAE, a new distributional contrastive disentanglement approach, along with a new contrastive loss and a new swap-reconstruction loss.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance on fairness, pretrained model debiasing, and domain generalization tasks across tabular, image, and text modalities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fair representation learning is important for fairness and debiasing sensitive information.
Adversarial approaches may train unstably and compromise the fairness-predictiveness balance.
FarconVAE separates sensitive and non-sensitive latent factors through distributional contrastive disentanglement.
The method uses a kernel-motivated contrastive loss with theoretical analysis and a swap-reconstruction loss.
The authors report superior performance across fairness, debiasing, and domain-generalization tasks and multiple modalities.

source_observation.claim: The method contrasts distributions of sensitive and non-sensitive latent representations while using same-label, different-sensitive-attribute pairs.

interpretation.claim: Pair construction and distribution-level objectives are used jointly to encourage disentanglement.

application.claim: When designing fair representations, consider supervision that holds labels constant while varying sensitive attributes and explicitly separates latent roles.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works when suitable same-label, different-sensitive-attribute pairs are unavailable.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
Theoretical assumptions and guarantees are not described.
Training stability is not independently evaluated in the abstract.
Implementation and reproducibility details are absent.
